study type: Secondary analysis of the Consortium on Safe Labor Database
exposure: Cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing
outcome: Composite adverse neonatal outcome (intraventricular hemorrhage grade III or IV, seizures, mechanical ventilation, sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis 2 or 3, or neonatal death)
Composite adverse maternal outcome (postpartum hemorrhage, endometritis, blood transfusion, chorioamnionitis, admission to intensive care unit, thromboembolism, or death)
cohort: 29,592 preterm births (23.0 to 36.6 weeks gestation) from the Consortium on Safe Labor Database, with 16,679 laboring for at least 2 hours.
finding: Preterm births undergoing cesarean delivery for non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing had a 59% higher risk of composite adverse neonatal outcomes compared to those with reassuring tracing.
